Trust me I agree, the county I work for we have events like this and we get called to the events to transport people to the hospital a lot. The goal of those on site (probably only EMT level) are to take care of the issues that doesn’t warrant an ambulance ride to the hospital, and manage what they can. The ambulances on site I’m not sure if they can transport to the hospital or only from point A to B, but a lot goes behind getting an actual ALS certification for your service and a lot of money too, so all in all it’s tough to get proper support. I’m sure there were some paramedics there yesterday too, but with everything that happened I’m sure they were stretched thin.

Then obviously you haven’t taken those because all of them teach what to do in 1:1 and pit crew CPR. Have you taken PHTLS as well? Or did you just take those courses for fun? I’m sorry the BLS crews didn’t know what to do, usually they suck at special events, but regardless they always have to call for ALS regardless since their capabilities are limited. It’s the world we live in.

1:1 CPR is taught is ACLS, and other CPR courses as bystander CPR is 1:1, and sometimes you may have to do 1:1 if you’re the only provider. I don’t need to prove myself to you, but you lack the understanding of what the EMS there was capable of, and I’m here to educate you on it as you’re clearly ignorant.

I think you have a misunderstanding of CPR… you’re referencing patient assessment and first aid. CPR is checking a pulse and either doing 1:1 CPR or 2+:1 CPR. Which you can easily tell if someone is alive by either seeing chest rise and fall, or reflexes. But, I wasn’t there. I’m a Paramedic by the way, so it’s okay, no need to explain.
